notes:
**Status: pending approval by Christian.** CHR-925 / CHR-907.

**Decision: toast, not banner.** A non-modal toast, bottom-right of the canvas area (right 296px = 280px right panel + 16, bottom 16px). It is `position:absolute` over the stage, so it does not move any layout: the topbar (44), variant bar (36) and panel widths are fixed and the canvas frame sizing/zoom depends on the stage height — a banner row would shift the whole canvas by its height each time it appears or is dismissed. A toast is also calm (one dismissible item, no layout jump, no modal), and the persistent, discoverable copy of the same information lives in the settings menu "About" row (see `shell-settings-menu` notes), so dismissing the toast loses nothing.

**Anatomy.** 360px wide, padding 12 (right 8), radius.md 10, `chrome-raised`, `chrome-shadow-float`, z 10, `role=status` (announced politely, never steals focus). Row: `upgrade` icon 20px `chrome-accent`; column with title "Artisign 2.2.0 is available" (13px medium) and `chrome-code-field` `compact` (28px, mono 12px) `artisign update` with a copy button (`content_copy` -> `check`); close `chrome-icon-btn` sm (`close`) top right, tooltip "Hide for today" (drawn above the button, shown here in hover state).

**Behaviour.** Appears once per page load when the daemon reports a newer version; close hides it until the next calendar day (browser-local, stored with the version so a newer release shows it again); no auto-dismiss timer; not shown when the update check is off. Clicking the code chip or the copy icon copies the command only — no update button (updating is a terminal action, `artisign update` restarts the daemon). Dark: same markup with the dark token group at the root.
